heroHeadline: Day 384: India's Pakistan Isolation Strategy Under Scrutiny — 15 km Border Demolition Drive, UNSC Rebukes, and Al Jazeera Analysis Assess Post-Sindoor Standoff
heroSubtitle: May 29, 2026: A major Al Jazeera analysis published today assessed that India's strategy to diplomatically isolate Pakistan has 'backfired in a big way' — with Islamabad gaining global clout through Pakistan's role in brokering the US-Iran ceasefire (April 2026), Shehbaz Sharif's four-day China state visit (May 23–26, CPEC 2.0 signed), and deepened US-Pakistan strategic ties under Trump. Meanwhile, India delivered a sharp UNSC rebuke on May 27–28 warning Pakistan 'will have to accept consequences of terrorism sponsorship,' while Home Minister Amit Shah ordered demolition of all structures within 15 km of the Pakistan border. On the water front, India is accelerating the Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel in Himachal Pradesh — part of a cumulative upstream hydraulic strategy analysts are calling the 'next India-Pakistan flashpoint.' The ceasefire holds at Day 384 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. The bilateral freeze continues: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT suspended and India's 'null and void' rejection of the PCA's May 15 award still operative.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
